epics.name: 264 SFS [Trust] Feature Toggle Cleanup
epics.description: 264 SFS [Trust] Feature Toggle Cleanup Dedicated epic for the 264-cycle feature toggle cleanup effort — carry-over from W-21962794 ( * [262][Trust][Scheduling Intelligence] , Closed). Spawned from the FT plan documented in docs/LLM/o2-workspace/docs/LLM/264/ft/README.md . Author: Guy Eden · Owner: Yonatan Bar-Yehuda · Quality: Irad Ben Dosa One-sentence summary We are simplifying version-gated feature toggles in the O2 stack by agreeing on MpVersion 258.0.0 as the floor for production traffic, which lets us delete roughly two-thirds of the toggle predicates and remove the matching if (FT.isEnabled()) branches from 5 Java repos. Why it matters Reduced complexity. Every FT predicate is a live branch in production. 25 of them have been effectively always-on for ~6 months and are now dead weight. Deleting them cuts regression-surface area in the request and response translators. Clearer version contract. MpVersion and CoreApiVersion flow from the caller as HTTP headers → RequestContextDTO (app-infra) → MDC → FeatureToggle.isFeatureEnabled(...) . Each service parses them independently; the MpVersion ↔ CoreApiVersion mapping lives in the external FT service, not in O2 source. Fewer predicates means fewer places where a mismatch can produce a silent misfire. Unblocks v262+ work. Features gated FROM 262.0.0 ( ExcludeArrivalWindowRulesForReshuffle , ScheduleOperationRemoveTasksFromGanttBug ) need a matching CoreApiVersion(67) predicate added. Doing that while the table is still cluttered with stale 238.3 / 240.x / 244 gates was not defensible. Phases — what's done, what's in flight, what's planned Done in 262 ( W-21962794 , Closed) Existing-status enumeration: 39 features × 4 prod regions, predicates documented per region. Splunk validation that production traffic is at MpVersion ≥ 258.0.0 across all 4 regions. Automation scripts: utils/promote_to_enable.py (Playwright-driven 25-feature × 4-region console flip with backup JSON) and utils/backout_to_custom.py (revert tool with dry-run-by-default). Pre-flip JSON dumps of all 4 prod regions ( jsons/ft_prod{1,3,4,8}_*.json ). FeatureToggleConfig.json 258-floor sweep — landed in common #3132 . In flight (4 PRs, console-flip side) | Repo | PR | Scope | |---|---|---| | o2service-common | #3132 | ABRequiredTimeZoneParam, TerritoryOptimizationRequestNewFields, ReadonlyFSLEndpoint, ComplexWorkAdvanced header, FeatureToggleConfig.json 258-floor | | o2-data-translator-service | #969 | 10 Easy features: ScheduleMode, ComplexWorkSlidingOverLunchBreak, CustomerLabelsParametersEnhancement, KeepScheduledServices, OffsetInSeconds, EnableReshuffleOnScheduleAndAB, ABRequiredTimeZoneParam, AllowOvertimeImprovements, AllowOvertimeInMiddleOfShift, PreferGPUEngine | | o2-fetch-data-service | #421 | ComplexWorkAdvanced, ParallelMSW | | o2service | #3126 | FillResourceGapsRequest, KeepScheduledServices (svc side) | To-do — 10 carry-over child stories under THIS epic Total story points: 23 (≈ XL T-shirt for the FT cleanup portion). Sequencing rules Console flips before code cleanup. Removing a source-side branch first would force the enabled path for any sub-258 client. 5-day observation window between flipping the console in all 4 regions and merging the per-feature code-cleanup PRs. Hard features ( ResourceContinuousAvailability , SALifeCycle ) get dedicated PRs with human integration testing. Yaml model regen runs only after the matching if (FT.isEnabled()) branches are gone. Operational artifacts Forward script: python docs/LLM/264/ft/utils/promote_to_enable.py --env prod{1,3,4,8} — 25-feature × 1-region console flip per run. Back-out script (immediate): python docs/LLM/264/ft/utils/backout_to_custom.py --env prod1 --apply . Recommended sequencing: dev4 → perf1 → test1 → (observe) → prod1 → prod3 → prod4 → prod8 . Stakeholders Implementor: Guy Eden Validator: Yonatan Bar-Yehuda QA Engineer: Irad Ben Dosa Approver / Code review: Orelie Fridler + team

epics.name: [266][SFS Mobile Assets][iOS] Notifications Priority
epics.description: Description (The "What") This epic involves implementing a tiered notification system for the AAA ACE iOS application. It introduces different notification priorities to differentiate "Current Work" (Dispatched/In-Progress) from "Scheduled Work" and "Routine Updates." This includes different audio, unique haptic (vibration) patterns, configurable display, and the ability for technicians to opt-in to break through Focus / "Do Not Disturb" for critical job changes. Benefits/Goals (The "Why") What customer problem does this solve? It solves Notification Fatigue . Currently, all alerts sound the same, causing technicians to ignore their phones. This leads to missed cancellations or address changes while the tech is "En-Route," resulting in wasted fuel and time. What data, customer insight, or business trend makes this feature important and timely? With a workforce of 8,000 technicians, even a small percentage of missed "Canceled" alerts represents a massive operational cost. The goal is to reduce missed critical notifications by 50% and ensure a response time of < 2 minutes for active jobs. Target Customer/Persona (The "Who") Field Technicians using iOS mobile devices (iPhone). Customer Outcomes / High-Level Requirements Sensory Differentiation: Technicians can identify a high-priority job update by sound and vibration alone, without looking at the screen. Critical Bypass: Users have the option to ensure critical work updates break through Focus / "Do Not Disturb" settings. User Scenarios in Scope As a technician driving to a job , I want a unique "Priority" sound to play if the job is canceled, so I can pull over safely or stop driving immediately. As a technician in a loud environment , I want a distinct vibration pattern for Dispatched jobs so I can feel the urgency even if I can't hear the phone. As a technician on a break , I want routine sync notifications to use the default sound so I am not unnecessarily interrupted. Out of Scope (i.e. Non-Goals) Android Support: This release is strictly for the iOS platform. Text-to-Speech: Read-aloud functionality for notification bodies is deferred. Logic Changes: No changes to the FSL "Drip-Feed" dispatching logic itself. Testing Hardware Diversity: Test haptic patterns across various iPhone models to ensure "perceptible difference." State Testing: Verify that notifications correctly transition from "Default" to "Priority" sounds the moment a Service Appointment status changes to "Dispatched." OS Compatibility: Ensure full functionality across the supported iOS version range (minimum supported iOS through the latest current version). Acceptance Criteria Priority Trigger: Unique sound/haptic triggers only for Service Appointments and Work Orders in the "Dispatched" or "In-Progress" status category. Default Fallback: All other app notifications (e.g., data sync, future schedule updates) must use the system default settings. User Control: Technicians must be able to toggle sounds/haptics off via iOS Settings > Notifications for the app. Performance: Custom sounds must fire within 1 second of the notification being received by the device.

epics.description: Field users on iOS cannot share device logs when they don't use Apple Mail — the app ignores their default email client (e.g. Outlook) and dead-ends them with "You must have email enabled on your device to use this feature." This blocks customers such as CONA Services (Signature, critical case), whose users are corporate-locked to Outlook and use log-sharing for their own internal troubleshooting. Apple Mail not configured → launch the OS share sheet; the user picks any email app (e.g. Gmail), the device logs are attached, and the user enters the recipient and sends. Done. Design: Figma — iOS Share Logs . In scope: gate Report an Issue on whether Apple Mail is configured; OS share-sheet fallback when it is not (reuse existing LogSharingManager on iOS); full device logs + existing context/body text attached; Android parity on the same "use the native mail client if configured, else the share sheet" decision; feature flag / kill switch to disable if needed; Splunk telemetry capturing when users share via a non-default-mail app (selected app/activity type + success/cancel, no log contents or PII). Out of scope: the iOS copy-email guidance pop-up (dropped — the earlier plan to copy the Salesforce feedback address for pasting into the TO field is no longer needed; on the share-sheet path the user enters the recipient in their chosen app); auto-case creation on the share-sheet path; changes to the existing Apple Mail path; separating "share logs" from "share feedback" (future direction). Security review: required. Potential data-exposure concerns were identified (full device logs can now be sent to any email app and to a user-entered recipient), so a review is tracked by W-23946603. Per Security (Riley MacDonald, 17 Aug 2026): answer the 9 questions in the C360 SA Template and theme this epic "Security Engagement Requested". Open: release/backport (266 vs 264 patch), final CX copy, MDM validation that Outlook surfaces in the share sheet. Source: #sfs-share-logs-improvements; CONA case in #support-sfs-mobile-tmp-swarm.

epics.description: Migrate the Record Edit test suite in FieldService-iOS from XCTest (XCTestCase / XCTAssert / setUpWithError) to the Swift Testing framework (import Testing / @Suite struct / @Test / #expect / #require), matching the pattern already adopted across ~100 files in the repo (e.g. WorkPlansListDataControllerTests, WorkPlans* suites). Each description follows the GUS user-story format (User Story → Background → Acceptance Criteria → Automation Approach → Assets → Dependencies → DoD → Cross-cutting/DoR → Estimate & Owner) and is written to be Claude-executable . The work items WI Work Item Title Auto Depends on Gates WI-1 W-23157720 Export & triage the 179 P0–P2 WOO scenarios (prune obsolete/duplicate) High — WI-2, WI-4 WI-2 W-23157729 Cross-reference scenarios vs existing iOS/Android tests; mark already-covered Automated High WI-1 WI-4, WI-7 WI-3 W-23157736 Q2 view-model coverage audit (iOS dashboard + Android equiv) High — (parallel) WI-4 WI-4 W-23157744 Classify remaining scenarios → Q1/Q2/must-be-Q3, naming target code Med WI-2, WI-3 WI-5, WI-6 WI-5 W-23157753 Design the 3–5 Maestro parent flows for the WOO seam Low (human) WI-4 WI-7 WI-6 W-23157811 Author Q1/Q2 tests for push-down candidates; mark automated Med WI-4 — WI-7 W-23157817 Author Maestro flows; re-automate legacy 27; obsolete superseded Med WI-5, WI-2 — WI-8 W-23157823 Review checkpoint with [reviewer] to validate strategy + samples Low (human gate) WI-1..WI-5 WI-6, WI-7, bulk writes Suggested sequence: WI-1 → (WI-2 ∥ WI-3) → WI-4 → WI-5 → WI-8 sign-off → (WI-6 ∥ WI-7). The only file with real data today is WI-1_woo_p0-p2_scenarios.csv (the live 179-scenario export) and its WI-1_scenarios_with_ids.csv (179/179 record Ids resolved). WI-1..WI-7 completed this loop; WI-8 was authored directly in the same format. We start from 179 priority (P0–P2) test scenarios and move each one to the cheapest place it can live: delete the dead ones, recognize the ones already covered by code, push what we can down to fast developer tests, and reserve a handful of full end-to-end tests for the journeys that truly need them. Most of the analysis work is automatable — Claude does the heavy lifting and a human approves before anything is changed for real. WI-1 — Clean up the test list. Produce one agreed, de-duplicated, pruned working set of the 179 scenarios so every later step builds on the same clean foundation. Obsolete tests are flagged (they can't be deleted, only retired) and near-duplicates are grouped for a merge decision. Output: a reviewed triage worksheet. WI-2 — Find what we already test. Cross-reference each surviving scenario against the existing iOS and Android code, so anything already verified by a real, current test is marked "automated" with the exact covering test recorded. Output: a coverage map. WI-3 — Measure mid-level coverage. Run an automated, repeatable audit of which Work Order Overview screens already have "Q2" (developer integration) test coverage, so the next step starts from facts rather than guesses about where the real gaps are. Output: a coverage gap list. WI-4 — Decide where each test belongs. Classify every remaining scenario into the lowest, cheapest test level that can still prove it — naming the specific piece of code each test should target — so the build steps get an unambiguous to-do list. Output: a per-scenario build list. WI-5 — Design the end-to-end tests. Consolidate the scenarios that genuinely need full end-to-end coverage into just 3–5 "parent" flows , each a realistic customer journey through the overview screen. This is the key design judgment (and the natural point to review with the senior QE). Output: flow designs. WI-6 — Build the fast tests. Turn WI-4's push-down candidates into real, merged, passing unit/integration tests on each platform, and only mark a scenario "automated" in the system after its test is actually merged. Output: merged tests + updated records. WI-7 — Build the end-to-end tests. Implement WI-5's flow designs as real, passing automated UI tests (Maestro) that run in our nightly pipeline, re-build the ~27 tests still running on the old framework, and retire the individual scenarios each new flow replaces — again, only once the test is merged and green. This is the largest item and a candidate to split by platform. Output: merged end-to-end flows + updated records. WI-8 — The sign-off gate. A single checkpoint where the senior QE ([reviewer]) reviews and approves the cleanup, coverage, classification, and flow design from WI-1–WI-5 before any records are changed in bulk or any test-building begins. Nothing irreversible happens until this sign-off is recorded. Output: a review packet + recorded approval.

epics.name: Core: Emergency-Dispatch Notification tier signal (264, Android + iOS)
epics.description: When a Service Appointment with IsEmergency = true is dispatched, Core delivers that dispatch notification at the Emergency tier (one of three fixed tiers: Standard / High / Emergency) so the mobile app renders it with emergency treatment. In 264 Core produces only the Standard and Emergency tiers, on both Android (FCM) and iOS (APNS). MECHANISM — RE-TIER, NOT A SECOND NOTIFICATION. Core keeps emitting the same dispatch notification and resolves its tier to Emergency when the gate below is true; it does not send a second push and suppress the first. This satisfies "one notification, not two — never flash the standard first" for free, because only one notification is ever produced. Core signals the tier in the push payload; the app renders the alert (sound/haptics/visual are app-owned — see cross-team dependency). PLATFORM-NEUTRAL CONTRACT. The tier is carried as sfdc.tier in the push payload, which already serves both FCM (Android) and APNS (iOS) — so the tier signal, the trigger gate, and per-recipient resolution are single-implementation and cover both platforms. The only platform-specific piece is the transport-priority gate: FCM high-priority on Android and its APNS equivalent (interruption level / priority) on iOS, both gated on the Emergency tier. TRIGGER GATE (resolved per recipient, in the async delivery handler, off the Service Appointment the message already carries): new Emergency-Dispatch setting = ON (read against the RECIPIENT's profile) AND ServiceAppointment.IsEmergency = true AND ServiceAppointment is (or was) Dispatched AND the event is a resource ASSIGNMENT (ENTITY_CREATED), not an un-assignment -> resolve tier = EMERGENCY (else STANDARD) The Emergency alert is INDEPENDENT of the standard dispatch-notification setting (IsDispatchNotification): it fires even when the technician has routine dispatch notifications turned off. It is gated only by its own new opt-in setting, which is DEFAULT OFF — so the feature is strictly additive and nothing changes on upgrade until an admin enables it per profile. Tier is resolved once in the delivery handler (producer-agnostic, FLS-safe, nothing carried across the async boundary) and carried to the device as sfdc.tier; the Emergency tier sets high transport priority (FCM high on Android, the APNS equivalent on iOS) so the device wakes promptly. CORE SCOPE (264): new per-profile admin setting (default OFF); enqueue emergency candidates past both dispatch-producer drop-gates; resolve the tier per recipient in the delivery handler and bridge it onto the notification; carry the tier onto the push payload (FCM + APNS) and gate high-priority on Emergency on both transports. DESIGN CONTRACTS: - Emergency tier is resolved at DISPATCH TIME ONLY. A later change to IsEmergency on an already-dispatched appointment does not retroactively fire or downgrade the alert. - Un-assigning a resource from an emergency appointment stays Standard. - Multi-recipient dispatch is evaluated per recipient against each recipient's own profile; a crew recipient receives the Standard notification and is never dropped. - Fail-open: if the IsEmergency read is ever inconclusive, resolve toward sending the alert. EXPLICITLY NOT IN THIS EPIC: app-side rendering (see cross-team dependency); any Emergency-sound override (MDM or core-upload) — 264 ships the app's bundled default sound only; the High tier producer; per-notification telemetry / per-org "Emergency sent" count. CROSS-TEAM DEPENDENCY (parallel 264 workstream): app-side rendering on both platforms — sound, haptics, DND/Focus breakthrough, iOS Time-Sensitive interruption-level handling, visual tier marker — is FS Mobile app-team-owned and also targeted for 264 (both iOS and Android, per Sandeep). It consumes this epic's sfdc.tier contract; sequence so the core contract lands in time for the app teams to build against it. FORWARD-COMPAT (not a 264 blocker): the tier contract Core establishes here (getNotificationTier() + sfdc.tier, three tiers) should be reused by Mobile Core Services / UNS (TD-0319603) rather than a parallel path. Confirm before 266 planning. --- SOURCE: spike W-22914294 (Emergency Pulse Channel); PRD 264-notification-priority-prd.md (FR-001, FR-003, FR-005, FR-005a, FR-008). Associate with TD-0319625; link under parent epic Priority Notifications (a3QEE000002KmKH2A0). --- SUCCESS CRITERIA: 1. With the Emergency setting ON for the recipient's profile and an emergency Service Appointment dispatched, exactly one notification is delivered at the Emergency tier on both Android and iOS; the standard dispatch notification is never separately sent or visibly flashed first. 2. The Emergency alert fires even when the recipient's standard dispatch-notification setting is OFF (independent of IsDispatchNotification). 3. With the Emergency setting OFF (default), behavior is unchanged from today for every notification (strictly additive). 4. Tier is resolved at dispatch time only; a post-dispatch change to IsEmergency does not retroactively fire or downgrade the alert. 5. Un-assigning a resource from an emergency appointment does not fire at the Emergency tier. 6. Assign-then-dispatch of an emergency appointment in one transaction yields exactly one Emergency notification, not two (verified by functional test). 7. The resolved tier is carried as sfdc.tier in both the FCM and APNS payloads; the Emergency tier sets high transport priority on both. 8. Each recipient on a multi-recipient dispatch is evaluated independently; a crew recipient receives the Standard notification and is never dropped.

epics.name: 266 SFS Mobile - [AA] Migrate Google Maps Directions/Matrix to Routes API
epics.description: Migrate Appointment Assistant's usage of the Google Maps Platform legacy Directions API and Distance Matrix API to the newer Routes API and Routes Matrix API. BACKGROUND Google Maps Platform is sunsetting the legacy Directions & Distance Matrix APIs in favor of the re-architected Routes & Routes Matrix APIs. Per the migration doc, Appointment Assistant and the SFS Android app are the two identified consumers of the legacy APIs. - Formal Deprecation: H1 2026 (legacy APIs move to Maintenance Mode - P0 bug fixes only, no new features). - Service Degradation: H1 2027 (earliest). - Full Discontinuation: 2028 or later (legacy APIs no longer callable). Google is actively pushing customers to migrate ahead of these dates. SCOPE (Appointment Assistant) - Inventory all AA calls to the Directions and Distance Matrix APIs. - Implement the Routes API / Routes Matrix API behind a feature flag in a Beta build; keep legacy API in production during a trial period and compare results. - Implement field masking (request only needed fields, e.g. routes.duration, routes.distanceMeters) to optimize payload size, performance, and cost. - Gradually cut over traffic to the Routes API, starting with lower-priority flows. RELATED WORK - Android equivalent: W-21809401 '[Android] Replace Google Maps API' (User Story, team SFS Mobile Location and DC, tag 'SFS - Mobile - Maps', under epic '266 SFS Mobile - [Trust] SFS Planned Trust Enhancements'). - Product tag for AA child stories: 'SFS Mobile App - Appointment Assistant' REFERENCES - Migration doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1wOPO_ZtWV2yEYJ8iNHrPlppAuyiVnv0Z5huJ8HpxWBI/edit - Why migrate: https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/routes/migrate-routes-why - How to migrate (technical): https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/routes/migrate-routes - Google POC: Jon Fusco - AA POC: Adi Sharet

Dependencies DI Inversion (Phase 2, High, XL) — CRITICAL PATH; break the 449-line god object so lower layers stop referencing concrete UI Dependencies. 4. epics.name: 264 SFS [Trust] Feature Toggle Cleanup
epics.description: 264 SFS [Trust] Feature Toggle Cleanup Dedicated epic for the 264-cycle feature toggle cleanup effort — carry-over from W-21962794 ( * [262][Trust][Scheduling Intelligence] , Closed). Spawned from the FT plan documented in docs/LLM/o2-workspace/docs/LLM/264/ft/README.md . Author: Guy Eden · Owner: Yonatan Bar-Yehuda · Quality: Irad Ben Dosa One-sentence summary We are simplifying version-gated feature toggles in the O2 stack by agreeing on MpVersion 258.0.0 as the floor for production traffic, which lets us delete roughly two-thirds of the toggle predicates and remove the matching if (FT.isEnabled()) branches from 5 Java repos. Why it matters Reduced complexity. Every FT predicate is a live branch in production. 25 of them have been effectively always-on for ~6 months and are now dead weight. Deleting them cuts regression-surface area in the request and response translators. Clearer version contract. MpVersion and CoreApiVersion flow from the caller as HTTP headers → RequestContextDTO (app-infra) → MDC → FeatureToggle.isFeatureEnabled(...) . Each service parses them independently; the MpVersion ↔ CoreApiVersion mapping lives in the external FT service, not in O2 source. Fewer predicates means fewer places where a mismatch can produce a silent misfire. Unblocks v262+ work. Features gated FROM 262.0.0 ( ExcludeArrivalWindowRulesForReshuffle , ScheduleOperationRemoveTasksFromGanttBug ) need a matching CoreApiVersion(67) predicate added. Doing that while the table is still cluttered with stale 238.3 / 240.x / 244 gates was not defensible. Phases — what's done, what's in flight, what's planned Done in 262 ( W-21962794 , Closed) Existing-status enumeration: 39 features × 4 prod regions, predicates documented per region. Splunk validation that production traffic is at MpVersion ≥ 258.0.0 across all 4 regions. Automation scripts: utils/promote_to_enable.py (Playwright-driven 25-feature × 4-region console flip with backup JSON) and utils/backout_to_custom.py (revert tool with dry-run-by-default). Pre-flip JSON dumps of all 4 prod regions ( jsons/ft_prod{1,3,4,8}_*.json ). FeatureToggleConfig.json 258-floor sweep — landed in common #3132 . In flight (4 PRs, console-flip side) | Repo | PR | Scope | |---|---|---| | o2service-common | #3132 | ABRequiredTimeZoneParam, TerritoryOptimizationRequestNewFields, ReadonlyFSLEndpoint, ComplexWorkAdvanced header, FeatureToggleConfig.json 258-floor | | o2-data-translator-service | #969 | 10 Easy features: ScheduleMode, ComplexWorkSlidingOverLunchBreak, CustomerLabelsParametersEnhancement, KeepScheduledServices, OffsetInSeconds, EnableReshuffleOnScheduleAndAB, ABRequiredTimeZoneParam, AllowOvertimeImprovements, AllowOvertimeInMiddleOfShift, PreferGPUEngine | | o2-fetch-data-service | #421 | ComplexWorkAdvanced, ParallelMSW | | o2service | #3126 | FillResourceGapsRequest, KeepScheduledServices (svc side) | To-do — 10 carry-over child stories under THIS epic Total story points: 23 (≈ XL T-shirt for the FT cleanup portion). Sequencing rules Console flips before code cleanup. Removing a source-side branch first would force the enabled path for any sub-258 client. 5-day observation window between flipping the console in all 4 regions and merging the per-feature code-cleanup PRs. Hard features ( ResourceContinuousAvailability , SALifeCycle ) get dedicated PRs with human integration testing. Yaml model regen runs only after the matching if (FT.isEnabled()) branches are gone. Operational artifacts Forward script: python docs/LLM/264/ft/utils/promote_to_enable.py --env prod{1,3,4,8} — 25-feature × 1-region console flip per run. Back-out script (immediate): python docs/LLM/264/ft/utils/backout_to_custom.py --env prod1 --apply . Recommended sequencing: dev4 → perf1 → test1 → (observe) → prod1 → prod3 → prod4 → prod8 . [266][SFS Mobile Assets][Android] Notifications Priority
epics.description: Description (The "What") This epic involves implementing a tiered notification system for the AAA ACE Android application. It introduces differnet notifications priority to differentiate "Current Work" (Dispatched/In-Progress) from "Scheduled Work" and "Routine Updates." This includes different audio, unique haptic (vibration) patterns, configurable display, and the ability for technicians to opt-in to "Do Not Disturb" bypass for critical job changes. Benefits/Goals (The "Why") What customer problem does this solve? It solves Notification Fatigue . Currently, all alerts sound the same, causing technicians to ignore their phones. This leads to missed cancellations or address changes while the tech is "En-Route," resulting in wasted fuel and time. What data, customer insight, or business trend makes this feature important and timely? With a workforce of 8,000 technicians, even a small percentage of missed "Canceled" alerts represents a massive operational cost. The goal is to reduce missed critical notifications by 50% and ensure a response time of < 2 minutes for active jobs. Target Customer/Persona (The "Who") Field Technicians using Android mobile devices . Customer Outcomes / High-Level Requirements Sensory Differentiation: Technicians can identify a high-priority job update by sound and vibration alone, without looking at the screen. Critical Bypass: Users have the option to ensure critical work updates break through "Do Not Disturb" settings. User Scenarios in Scope As a technician driving to a job , I want a unique "Priority" sound to play if the job is canceled, so I can pull over safely or stop driving immediately. As a technician in a loud environment , I want a distinct vibration pattern for Dispatched jobs so I can feel the urgency even if I can't hear the phone. As a technician on a break , I want routine sync notifications to use the default sound so I am not unnecessarily interrupted. Out of Scope (i.e. Non-Goals) iOS Support: This release is strictly for the Android platform. Text-to-Speech: Read-aloud functionality for notification bodies is deferred. Logic Changes: No changes to the FSL "Drip-Feed" dispatching logic itself. Testing Hardware Diversity: Test haptic patterns across various Android device models to ensure "perceptible difference." State Testing: Verify that notifications correctly transition from "Default" to "Priority" sounds the moment a Service Appointment status changes to "Dispatched." OS Compatibility: Ensure full functionality on Android 8.0 through the latest current version. Acceptance Criteria Priority Trigger: Unique sound/haptic triggers only for Service Appointments and Work Orders in the "Dispatched" or "In-Progress" status category. Default Fallback: All other app notifications (e.g., data sync, future schedule updates) must use the system default settings. User Control: Technicians must be able to toggle sounds/haptics off via the Android System Settings for the specific app channels. Performance: Custom sounds must fire within 1 second of the notification being received by the device.

epics.name: Share Logs — Open Email-App Sharing (iOS + Android)
epics.description: Field users on iOS cannot share device logs when they don't use Apple Mail — the app ignores their default email client (e.g. Outlook) and dead-ends them with "You must have email enabled on your device to use this feature." This blocks customers such as CONA Services (Signature, critical case), whose users are corporate-locked to Outlook and use log-sharing for their own internal troubleshooting. Agreed approach (#sfs-share-logs-improvements, 4 Aug 2026): rather than solving for multiple use cases (share-with-admin vs. share-with-support), which deteriorates the experience, we simplify to a single decision point on Report an Issue: Mobile user taps Report an Issue . SFS checks for Apple Mail. Apple Mail configured → continue with the existing flow (drill-in screen, tap the check mark, Apple Mail sheet pre-populated to mobilefieldservicefeedback@salesforce.com with logs attached, tap send). Apple Mail not configured → launch the OS share sheet; the user picks any email app (e.g. Gmail), the device logs are attached, and the user enters the recipient and sends. Done. epics.name: Core: Emergency-Dispatch Notification tier signal (264, Android + iOS)
epics.description: When a Service Appointment with IsEmergency = true is dispatched, Core delivers that dispatch notification at the Emergency tier (one of three fixed tiers: Standard / High / Emergency) so the mobile app renders it with emergency treatment. In 264 Core produces only the Standard and Emergency tiers, on both Android (FCM) and iOS (APNS). MECHANISM — RE-TIER, NOT A SECOND NOTIFICATION. Core keeps emitting the same dispatch notification and resolves its tier to Emergency when the gate below is true; it does not send a second push and suppress the first. This satisfies "one notification, not two — never flash the standard first" for free, because only one notification is ever produced. Core signals the tier in the push payload; the app renders the alert (sound/haptics/visual are app-owned — see cross-team dependency). PLATFORM-NEUTRAL CONTRACT. The tier is carried as sfdc.tier in the push payload, which already serves both FCM (Android) and APNS (iOS) — so the tier signal, the trigger gate, and per-recipient resolution are single-implementation and cover both platforms. The only platform-specific piece is the transport-priority gate: FCM high-priority on Android and its APNS equivalent (interruption level / priority) on iOS, both gated on the Emergency tier. TRIGGER GATE (resolved per recipient, in the async delivery handler, off the Service Appointment the message already carries): new Emergency-Dispatch setting = ON (read against the RECIPIENT's profile) AND ServiceAppointment.IsEmergency = true AND ServiceAppointment is (or was) Dispatched AND the event is a resource ASSIGNMENT (ENTITY_CREATED), not an un-assignment -> resolve tier = EMERGENCY (else STANDARD) The Emergency alert is INDEPENDENT of the standard dispatch-notification setting (IsDispatchNotification): it fires even when the technician has routine dispatch notifications turned off. It is gated only by its own new opt-in setting, which is DEFAULT OFF — so the feature is strictly additive and nothing changes on upgrade until an admin enables it per profile. Tier is resolved once in the delivery handler (producer-agnostic, FLS-safe, nothing carried across the async boundary) and carried to the device as sfdc.tier; the Emergency tier sets high transport priority (FCM high on Android, the APNS equivalent on iOS) so the device wakes promptly. CORE SCOPE (264): new per-profile admin setting (default OFF); enqueue emergency candidates past both dispatch-producer drop-gates; resolve the tier per recipient in the delivery handler and bridge it onto the notification; carry the tier onto the push payload (FCM + APNS) and gate high-priority on Emergency on both transports. DESIGN CONTRACTS: - Emergency tier is resolved at DISPATCH TIME ONLY. A later change to IsEmergency on an already-dispatched appointment does not retroactively fire or downgrade the alert. - Un-assigning a resource from an emergency appointment stays Standard. - Multi-recipient dispatch is evaluated per recipient against each recipient's own profile; a crew recipient receives the Standard notification and is never dropped. - Fail-open: if the IsEmergency read is ever inconclusive, resolve toward sending the alert. EXPLICITLY NOT IN THIS EPIC: app-side rendering (see cross-team dependency); any Emergency-sound override (MDM or core-upload) — 264 ships the app's bundled default sound only; the High tier producer; per-notification telemetry / per-org "Emergency sent" count. CROSS-TEAM DEPENDENCY (parallel 264 workstream): app-side rendering on both platforms — sound, haptics, DND/Focus breakthrough, iOS Time-Sensitive interruption-level handling, visual tier marker — is FS Mobile app-team-owned and also targeted for 264 (both iOS and Android, per Sandeep). It consumes this epic's sfdc.tier contract; sequence so the core contract lands in time for the app teams to build against it. FORWARD-COMPAT (not a 264 blocker): the tier contract Core establishes here (getNotificationTier() + sfdc.tier, three tiers) should be reused by Mobile Core Services / UNS (TD-0319603) rather than a parallel path. Confirm before 266 planning. --- SOURCE: spike W-22914294 (Emergency Pulse Channel); PRD 264-notification-priority-prd.md (FR-001, FR-003, FR-005, FR-005a, FR-008). Associate with TD-0319625; link under parent epic Priority Notifications (a3QEE000002KmKH2A0). --- SUCCESS CRITERIA: 1. With the Emergency setting ON for the recipient's profile and an emergency Service Appointment dispatched, exactly one notification is delivered at the Emergency tier on both Android and iOS; the standard dispatch notification is never separately sent or visibly flashed first. 2. The Emergency alert fires even when the recipient's standard dispatch-notification setting is OFF (independent of IsDispatchNotification). 3. With the Emergency setting OFF (default), behavior is unchanged from today for every notification (strictly additive). 4. Tier is resolved at dispatch time only; a post-dispatch change to IsEmergency does not retroactively fire or downgrade the alert. 5. Un-assigning a resource from an emergency appointment does not fire at the Emergency tier. 6. Assign-then-dispatch of an emergency appointment in one transaction yields exactly one Emergency notification, not two (verified by functional test). 7. The resolved tier is carried as sfdc.tier in both the FCM and APNS payloads; the Emergency tier sets high transport priority on both. 8. Each recipient on a multi-recipient dispatch is evaluated independently; a crew recipient receives the Standard notification and is never dropped.

epics.description: Migrate Appointment Assistant's usage of the Google Maps Platform legacy Directions API and Distance Matrix API to the newer Routes API and Routes Matrix API. BACKGROUND Google Maps Platform is sunsetting the legacy Directions & Distance Matrix APIs in favor of the re-architected Routes & Routes Matrix APIs. epics.description: 264 SFS [Trust] Feature Toggle Cleanup Dedicated epic for the 264-cycle feature toggle cleanup effort — carry-over from W-21962794 ( * [262][Trust][Scheduling Intelligence] , Closed). Spawned from the FT plan documented in docs/LLM/o2-workspace/docs/LLM/264/ft/README.md . Author: Guy Eden · Owner: Yonatan Bar-Yehuda · Quality: Irad Ben Dosa One-sentence summary We are simplifying version-gated feature toggles in the O2 stack by agreeing on MpVersion 258.0.0 as the floor for production traffic, which lets us delete roughly two-thirds of the toggle predicates and remove the matching if (FT.isEnabled()) branches from 5 Java repos. Why it matters Reduced complexity. Every FT predicate is a live branch in production. 25 of them have been effectively always-on for ~6 months and are now dead weight. Deleting them cuts regression-surface area in the request and response translators. Clearer version contract. MpVersion and CoreApiVersion flow from the caller as HTTP headers → RequestContextDTO (app-infra) → MDC → FeatureToggle.isFeatureEnabled(...) . Each service parses them independently; the MpVersion ↔ CoreApiVersion mapping lives in the external FT service, not in O2 source. Fewer predicates means fewer places where a mismatch can produce a silent misfire. Unblocks v262+ work. Features gated FROM 262.0.0 ( ExcludeArrivalWindowRulesForReshuffle , ScheduleOperationRemoveTasksFromGanttBug ) need a matching CoreApiVersion(67) predicate added. Doing that while the table is still cluttered with stale 238.3 / 240.x / 244 gates was not defensible. Phases — what's done, what's in flight, what's planned Done in 262 ( W-21962794 , Closed) Existing-status enumeration: 39 features × 4 prod regions, predicates documented per region. Splunk validation that production traffic is at MpVersion ≥ 258.0.0 across all 4 regions. Automation scripts: utils/promote_to_enable.py (Playwright-driven 25-feature × 4-region console flip with backup JSON) and utils/backout_to_custom.py (revert tool with dry-run-by-default). Pre-flip JSON dumps of all 4 prod regions ( jsons/ft_prod{1,3,4,8}_*.json ). FeatureToggleConfig.json 258-floor sweep — landed in common #3132 . In flight (4 PRs, console-flip side) | Repo | PR | Scope | |---|---|---| | o2service-common | #3132 | ABRequiredTimeZoneParam, TerritoryOptimizationRequestNewFields, ReadonlyFSLEndpoint, ComplexWorkAdvanced header, FeatureToggleConfig.json 258-floor | | o2-data-translator-service | #969 | 10 Easy features: ScheduleMode, ComplexWorkSlidingOverLunchBreak, CustomerLabelsParametersEnhancement, KeepScheduledServices, OffsetInSeconds, EnableReshuffleOnScheduleAndAB, ABRequiredTimeZoneParam, AllowOvertimeImprovements, AllowOvertimeInMiddleOfShift, PreferGPUEngine | | o2-fetch-data-service | #421 | ComplexWorkAdvanced, ParallelMSW | | o2service | #3126 | FillResourceGapsRequest, KeepScheduledServices (svc side) | To-do — 10 carry-over child stories under THIS epic Total story points: 23 (≈ XL T-shirt for the FT cleanup portion). Sequencing rules Console flips before code cleanup. Removing a source-side branch first would force the enabled path for any sub-258 client. 5-day observation window between flipping the console in all 4 regions and merging the per-feature code-cleanup PRs. Hard features ( ResourceContinuousAvailability , SALifeCycle ) get dedicated PRs with human integration testing. Yaml model regen runs only after the matching if (FT.isEnabled()) branches are gone. Operational artifacts Forward script: python docs/LLM/264/ft/utils/promote_to_enable.py --env prod{1,3,4,8} — 25-feature × 1-region console flip per run. Back-out script (immediate): python docs/LLM/264/ft/utils/backout_to_custom.py --env prod1 --apply . Recommended sequencing: dev4 → perf1 → test1 → (observe) → prod1 → prod3 → prod4 → prod8 . Stakeholders Implementor: Guy Eden Validator: Yonatan Bar-Yehuda QA Engineer: Irad Ben Dosa Approver / Code review: Orelie Fridler + team

epics.name: [AGX GA] Iteration of Steps
epics.description: Synopsis: Allows an AGX flow to dynamically loop through a series of steps based on a collection of Salesforce records (such as multiple Work Order Line Items), enabling the completion of multiple goals within a single appointment. Acceptance Criteria: Admins must be able to define an iterator within their AGX configuration that establishes which steps and decisions repeat for each item in the data collection. Mobile users must see a dynamic number of screens reflecting the goals present for that specific job. Basic Testing Criteria: Assign a job that has multiple child records associated with it. Ensure the guided flow correctly repeats the assigned iteration loop for every individual child record before permitting the user to proceed to the next stage.

epics.name: [AGX GA] Optional Actions
epics.description: Synopsis: Provides mobile workers with a curated list of optional actions (like launching Data Capture Forms, Quick Actions, or Screen Flows) available throughout the job to handle unplanned deviations without leaving the guided experience. Acceptance Criteria: Admins can configure the order, naming, and availability of both global and record-based actions in this list, incorporating custom business logic to define which records launch the actions. Mobile users can access these actions without needing to use the "escape hatch" to navigate the standard data model. Basic Testing Criteria: Configure an optional action list with a Quick Action and a Data Capture form. Initiate a job on mobile, open the optional actions menu mid-flow, execute an action, and verify the user seamlessly returns to their main job flow upon completion.

epics.name: [AGX GA] Parallel Steps
epics.description: Synopsis: Gives users the autonomy to complete different job steps simultaneously or in an unprescribed order (e.g., doing safety checks and parts checks), removing unnecessary linear restrictions that could cause inefficiency. Acceptance Criteria: Admins must be able to define steps that can be completed in parallel within the AGX Orchestration. Mobile users must be able to interact with and complete these steps in whatever order makes the most logical sense to them. Basic Testing Criteria: Set up an orchestration containing parallel steps. Access the job on a mobile device, complete the parallel steps in various sequences, and ensure that completion of the stage accurately reflects the fulfillment of all parallel steps.

epics.description: Migrate Appointment Assistant's usage of the Google Maps Platform legacy Directions API and Distance Matrix API to the newer Routes API and Routes Matrix API. BACKGROUND Google Maps Platform is sunsetting the legacy Directions & Distance Matrix APIs in favor of the re-architected Routes & Routes Matrix APIs. Per the migration doc, Appointment Assistant and the SFS Android app are the two identified consumers of the legacy APIs. - Formal Deprecation: H1 2026 (legacy APIs move to Maintenance Mode - P0 bug fixes only, no new features). - Service Degradation: H1 2027 (earliest). - Full Discontinuation: 2028 or later (legacy APIs no longer callable). Google is actively pushing customers to migrate ahead of these dates. SCOPE (Appointment Assistant) - Inventory all AA calls to the Directions and Distance Matrix APIs. - Implement the Routes API / Routes Matrix API behind a feature flag in a Beta build; keep legacy API in production during a trial period and compare results. - Implement field masking (request only needed fields, e.g. routes.duration, routes.distanceMeters) to optimize payload size, performance, and cost. - Gradually cut over traffic to the Routes API, starting with lower-priority flows. RELATED WORK - Android equivalent: W-21809401 '[Android] Replace Google Maps API' (User Story, team SFS Mobile Location and DC, tag 'SFS - Mobile - Maps', under epic '266 SFS Mobile - [Trust] SFS Planned Trust Enhancements'). - Product tag for AA child stories: 'SFS Mobile App - Appointment Assistant' REFERENCES - Migration doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1wOPO_ZtWV2yEYJ8iNHrPlppAuyiVnv0Z5huJ8HpxWBI/edit - Why migrate: https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/routes/migrate-routes-why - How to migrate (technical): https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/routes/migrate-routes - Google POC: Jon Fusco - AA POC: Adi Sharet

epics.name: Core: Emergency-Dispatch Notification tier signal (264, Android + iOS)
epics.description: When a Service Appointment with IsEmergency = true is dispatched, Core delivers that dispatch notification at the Emergency tier (one of three fixed tiers: Standard / High / Emergency) so the mobile app renders it with emergency treatment. In 264 Core produces only the Standard and Emergency tiers, on both Android (FCM) and iOS (APNS). MECHANISM — RE-TIER, NOT A SECOND NOTIFICATION. Core keeps emitting the same dispatch notification and resolves its tier to Emergency when the gate below is true; it does not send a second push and suppress the first. This satisfies "one notification, not two — never flash the standard first" for free, because only one notification is ever produced. Core signals the tier in the push payload; the app renders the alert (sound/haptics/visual are app-owned — see cross-team dependency). PLATFORM-NEUTRAL CONTRACT. The tier is carried as sfdc.tier in the push payload, which already serves both FCM (Android) and APNS (iOS) — so the tier signal, the trigger gate, and per-recipient resolution are single-implementation and cover both platforms. The only platform-specific piece is the transport-priority gate: FCM high-priority on Android and its APNS equivalent (interruption level / priority) on iOS, both gated on the Emergency tier. TRIGGER GATE (resolved per recipient, in the async delivery handler, off the Service Appointment the message already carries): new Emergency-Dispatch setting = ON (read against the RECIPIENT's profile) AND ServiceAppointment.IsEmergency = true AND ServiceAppointment is (or was) Dispatched AND the event is a resource ASSIGNMENT (ENTITY_CREATED), not an un-assignment -> resolve tier = EMERGENCY (else STANDARD) The Emergency alert is INDEPENDENT of the standard dispatch-notification setting (IsDispatchNotification): it fires even when the technician has routine dispatch notifications turned off. It is gated only by its own new opt-in setting, which is DEFAULT OFF — so the feature is strictly additive and nothing changes on upgrade until an admin enables it per profile. Tier is resolved once in the delivery handler (producer-agnostic, FLS-safe, nothing carried across the async boundary) and carried to the device as sfdc.tier; the Emergency tier sets high transport priority (FCM high on Android, the APNS equivalent on iOS) so the device wakes promptly. CORE SCOPE (264): new per-profile admin setting (default OFF); enqueue emergency candidates past both dispatch-producer drop-gates; resolve the tier per recipient in the delivery handler and bridge it onto the notification; carry the tier onto the push payload (FCM + APNS) and gate high-priority on Emergency on both transports. DESIGN CONTRACTS: - Emergency tier is resolved at DISPATCH TIME ONLY. A later change to IsEmergency on an already-dispatched appointment does not retroactively fire or downgrade the alert. - Un-assigning a resource from an emergency appointment stays Standard. - Multi-recipient dispatch is evaluated per recipient against each recipient's own profile; a crew recipient receives the Standard notification and is never dropped. - Fail-open: if the IsEmergency read is ever inconclusive, resolve toward sending the alert. EXPLICITLY NOT IN THIS EPIC: app-side rendering (see cross-team dependency); any Emergency-sound override (MDM or core-upload) — 264 ships the app's bundled default sound only; the High tier producer; per-notification telemetry / per-org "Emergency sent" count. CROSS-TEAM DEPENDENCY (parallel 264 workstream): app-side rendering on both platforms — sound, haptics, DND/Focus breakthrough, iOS Time-Sensitive interruption-level handling, visual tier marker — is FS Mobile app-team-owned and also targeted for 264 (both iOS and Android, per Sandeep). It consumes this epic's sfdc.tier contract; sequence so the core contract lands in time for the app teams to build against it. FORWARD-COMPAT (not a 264 blocker): the tier contract Core establishes here (getNotificationTier() + sfdc.tier, three tiers) should be reused by Mobile Core Services / UNS (TD-0319603) rather than a parallel path. Confirm before 266 planning. --- SOURCE: spike W-22914294 (Emergency Pulse Channel); PRD 264-notification-priority-prd.md (FR-001, FR-003, FR-005, FR-005a, FR-008). Associate with TD-0319625; link under parent epic Priority Notifications (a3QEE000002KmKH2A0). --- SUCCESS CRITERIA: 1. With the Emergency setting ON for the recipient's profile and an emergency Service Appointment dispatched, exactly one notification is delivered at the Emergency tier on both Android and iOS; the standard dispatch notification is never separately sent or visibly flashed first. 2. The Emergency alert fires even when the recipient's standard dispatch-notification setting is OFF (independent of IsDispatchNotification). 3. With the Emergency setting OFF (default), behavior is unchanged from today for every notification (strictly additive). 4. Tier is resolved at dispatch time only; a post-dispatch change to IsEmergency does not retroactively fire or downgrade the alert. 5. Un-assigning a resource from an emergency appointment does not fire at the Emergency tier. 6. Assign-then-dispatch of an emergency appointment in one transaction yields exactly one Emergency notification, not two (verified by functional test). 7. The resolved tier is carried as sfdc.tier in both the FCM and APNS payloads; the Emergency tier sets high transport priority on both. 8. Each recipient on a multi-recipient dispatch is evaluated independently; a crew recipient receives the Standard notification and is never dropped.

epics.name: Share Logs — Open Email-App Sharing (iOS + Android)
epics.description: Field users on iOS cannot share device logs when they don't use Apple Mail — the app ignores their default email client (e.g. Outlook) and dead-ends them with "You must have email enabled on your device to use this feature." This blocks customers such as CONA Services (Signature, critical case), whose users are corporate-locked to Outlook and use log-sharing for their own internal troubleshooting. Agreed approach (#sfs-share-logs-improvements, 4 Aug 2026): rather than solving for multiple use cases (share-with-admin vs. share-with-support), which deteriorates the experience, we simplify to a single decision point on Report an Issue: Mobile user taps Report an Issue . SFS checks for Apple Mail. Apple Mail configured → continue with the existing flow (drill-in screen, tap the check mark, Apple Mail sheet pre-populated to mobilefieldservicefeedback@salesforce.com with logs attached, tap send). Apple Mail not configured → launch the OS share sheet; the user picks any email app (e.g. Gmail), the device logs are attached, and the user enters the recipient and sends. Done. Design: Figma — iOS Share Logs . In scope: gate Report an Issue on whether Apple Mail is configured; OS share-sheet fallback when it is not (reuse existing LogSharingManager on iOS); full device logs + existing context/body text attached; Android parity on the same "use the native mail client if configured, else the share sheet" decision; feature flag / kill switch to disable if needed; Splunk telemetry capturing when users share via a non-default-mail app (selected app/activity type + success/cancel, no log contents or PII). Out of scope: the iOS copy-email guidance pop-up (dropped — the earlier plan to copy the Salesforce feedback address for pasting into the TO field is no longer needed; on the share-sheet path the user enters the recipient in their chosen app); auto-case creation on the share-sheet path; changes to the existing Apple Mail path; separating "share logs" from "share feedback" (future direction). Security review: required. Potential data-exposure concerns were identified (full device logs can now be sent to any email app and to a user-entered recipient), so a review is tracked by W-23946603. Per Security (Riley MacDonald, 17 Aug 2026): answer the 9 questions in the C360 SA Template and theme this epic "Security Engagement Requested". Open: release/backport (266 vs 264 patch), final CX copy, MDM validation that Outlook surfaces in the share sheet. Source: #sfs-share-logs-improvements; CONA case in #support-sfs-mobile-tmp-swarm.

epics.name: [iOS] [SFS Mobile Assets] Migrate Record Edit XCTest suite to Swift Testing
epics.description: Migrate the Record Edit test suite in FieldService-iOS from XCTest (XCTestCase / XCTAssert / setUpWithError) to the Swift Testing framework (import Testing / @Suite struct / @Test / #expect / #require), matching the pattern already adopted across ~100 files in the repo (e.g. WorkPlansListDataControllerTests, WorkPlans* suites). Scope: ~24 XCTest files under FieldServiceSDK/FieldServiceUITests/Classes/RecordEdit, plus FieldServiceSDK/FieldServiceSDKTests/Integration/Features/RecordEdit/RecordFormViewModelIntegrationTests.swift. LookupViewModelManagingTests.swift (SDKTests/Features/RecordEdit) is ALREADY on Swift Testing and is excluded. Broken into small per-file stories (with the 5,596-line RecordFormViewModelTests split into sub-stories by concern). Why: Swift Testing is the repo's standard going forward. Consolidating the Record Edit suite improves readability (#expect vs XCTAssert), enables parameterized tests and .tags/.serialized traits, removes Optional force-unwrap in setUp via TestContext.make(), and keeps the suite consistent with the rest of the codebase. Migration conventions (from existing migrated suites): - Replace `final class XTests: XCTestCase` with `@Suite("...", .tags(.recordEdit), .serialized) struct XTests` (add @MainActor where UI/main-actor bound). - Replace setUpWithError/tearDownWithError instance state with a `TestContext` struct + `static func make()` factory; construct per-test. - Replace XCTAssert* with #expect(...) and force-unwraps with try #require(...). - Replace XCTestExpectation/wait with async/await or confirmation { }. - Preserve Cuckoo / OCMockitoSwift / Hamcrest usage; keep test intent and coverage identical. Acceptance for the epic: all in-scope files migrated, no remaining `import XCTest` / `XCTestCase` in the RecordEdit test folders, full RecordEdit suite passes on CI, no loss of test coverage.

epics.name: [iOS] [SFS Mobile Assets] Reduce OOM Crashes - Field Service Mobile
epics.description: Reduce Out-Of-Memory (OOM) crashes in the Field Service iOS app via a set of small, low-risk, self-contained code changes identified by a codebase scan cross-referenced against Firebase Crashlytics (BigQuery) OOM signatures for fsl-firebase-prod. Scope = app-owned, fixable OOM sites only (excludes upstream/Apple frameworks: Nimbus, GeoServices, VectorKit, JavaScriptCore). Root-cause themes: 1. Full-directory/file-list materialization (getFolderSize using subpaths(atPath:)). 2. Full-resolution image decode + repeated re-rasterization on pick/compress. 3. Whole-page JSON decode during Advanced Priming network fetch (default pageSize=10000) - Android already routes this through an overridable PageSizeHolder; iOS hardcodes it. 4. Materializing entire log files on read. Each story is independently shippable and testable.
